A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same crowdsourcing study and intervention framework. Their main text, tables, figures, and appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original findings from 350 participants assessing and rewriting 700 LLM examples, including behavioral frequencies and an inventory of 28 intervention types.

after.justification: V2 retains these original crowdsourcing findings and adds descriptive statistics on agreement between participants in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The four-dimensional conceptual framework, 28 intervention types, and example operationalizations remain unchanged. Expanded coding explanations and revised attribution of existing interventions do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the same seven dataset groups: two PRISM groups, LMSys, DICES, and three UltraFeedback groups. The reported 700 examples, US-based English-speaking population, and assessment-and-rewriting task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing mitigation methods against a proposed algorithm. The literature inventory and newly listed source models do not constitute evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces an agreement metric counting examples with at least two of three positive ratings, conditional on at least one positive rating. Existing study settings are retained. The reference to three raters conflicts with Section 2.2's two raters per example, so additional annotation is not established.

E4.justification: V2 adds a supplementary analysis of participant agreement across five behavioral categories. Existing dataset breakdowns, participant-background analyses, and example rewrites in Figures A6–A7 and Table A5 are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B first reports descriptive interparticipant agreement estimates and specifies their positive-annotation denominator. No confidence intervals, significance tests, or additional annotation rounds are established.

E6.justification: Appendix B adds agreement fractions for cognition (0.20), feelings/opinions (0.36), physical actions (0.09), sense of self (0.24), and social skills (0.30). Section 3.2 also changes the number of crowdsourcing-only intervention types from 13 to 15. Existing behavioral frequencies and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B newly defines the conditional majority-agreement ratio through its numerator and denominator. This is a limited mathematical definition; the conceptual framework is retained and no proofs or formal guarantees are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and overarching contributions retain their scope. However, Section 3.2 and Table 4 increase the claimed crowdsourcing-only contribution from 13 to 15 intervention types within the unchanged 28-type inventory.

C2.justification: Section 4 replaces the accuracy-focused explanation of adding/removing uncertainty with a fuller account involving perceived objectivity and human-like equivocation. V2 also adds qualifications about post-study response priming, the absence of ground truth, and why dataset differences cannot establish differences between LLMs.

D1.justification: V2 newly describes responsibility for literature coding and consensus, adds source-model lists to Table A4, and discloses that sampling did not account for model identity. The character-length filter and much of the expanded coding procedure were already documented in v1's appendices.

R1.justification: Table 4 reclassifies adding source references and removing normative judgments as crowdsourcing-only interventions and adds explicit citations for literature-supported types. Table A1 revises supporting quotations and annotations within the retained literature sample. Reference-list changes otherwise update the same works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized rewrites and explanatory expansions in Sections 2 and 4, adds an agreement subsection in Appendix B, and edits author information and bibliographic text. The overall section structure and most narrative content remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains row-level citations and revised bold emphasis; Table A1 is reordered and reformatted; Table A4 gains a Models column. Appendix tables are restyled and relocated, and Figure A6's caption expands. All seven figures are retained with unchanged screenshots and plotted results.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 makes intervention provenance and dataset sources easier to audit and better qualifies interpretations through clearer coding documentation, Tables 4/A4, and expanded limitations. These provide a modest gain in transparency. The core evidence remains unchanged, and the new agreement analysis's unresolved two-versus-three-rater discrepancy limits the value of that addition.
